items.q: Single-pass or double-pass RO?
items.a: Single-pass RO and EDI suits moderate solids. Double pass adds margin on conductivity, TOC and silica, for high-solids feed or PW feeding a WFI still or pure steam generator.

items.q: How do you handle cold winter feed?
items.a: Rated at 25 °C, RO can lose a third or more of its output at 5 °C. We size at your coldest feed, or add a heat exchanger.

items.q: Our supply is chloraminated. What changes?
items.a: Chloramine damages RO membranes, so it is removed first, which releases ammonia. Ammonia can pass RO when pH is raised for CO₂ control, so we design both together.

items.q: Hot water or chemical sanitization?
items.a: Hot water leaves no residual to test for and is proven at the coldest point. Chemical sanitization suits membranes not rated for heat, but adds a residual test.

items.q: How do we know it will pass IQ/OQ?
items.a: Your quality unit approves the FAT protocol and witnesses a wet FAT, in person or remotely, before the skid ships. SAT and OQ then prove performance on your feed.

items.q: Who decides whether water already used is affected?
items.a: Your quality unit. Our signed service report gives it the facts: when readings left specification, what was affected, what we found and did. We do not release water.

items.q: We have no service plan. Will you come?
items.a: Yes, as a call-out with the next available technician, at [call-out rate and hourly rate, CAD].

items.q: Our IT allows no remote access to GMP equipment.
items.a: Choose "No remote connection". We diagnose from your readings, files and a call with your operators. On-site response times do not change.

items.q: Can you work to our SOPs, forms and induction?
items.a: Yes. Name them in "Site access requirements". We send training records with the visit plan and fill in your forms as well as, or instead of, ours.
